extracted.intended_audience: ProofWiki contributors and editors (users who want to create or edit ProofWiki pages)
extracted.subtask_description: Site-specific guidance for contributing to ProofWiki: how to test edits, discussion-page etiquette (signatures), the site's scope (a compendium of proofs), and pointers to the detailed help pages (editing, LaTeX, house style, templates, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sandbox
rubrics_metrics.description: The ProofWiki sandbox is a great place to test out your LaTeX and wiki skills without having to tamper with an actual page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the main sandbox for experiments; if you prefer a personal area you can create one at http://www.proofwiki.org/wiki/User:your_username/Sandbox. Test formatting, LaTeX, and edits there rather than on live pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion page signature etiquette
rubrics_metrics.description: When you post on a discussion page be sure to include your signature. This includes your username (with a link to your user page), and a timestamp of when the edit was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include your signature by pressing the signature button on the taskbar above the editing window (second button from the right) or insert it manually. Example wiki code/appearance: '~~~' produces 'User'; '~~~~' produces 'User 12:34, 1 January 2012 (UTC)'. Signatures are often preceded by -- (two dashes) to separate the signature from the text body, although this is not necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: ProofWiki scope (compendium of proofs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please note, however, that ProofWiki is a compendium of proofs, not an online math Q&A forum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributions should focus on definitions, statements, and full proofs rather than question-style posts or casual Q&A content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add items you can't prove yourself
rubrics_metrics.description: Have something that you think should be added but don't know how to prove yourself? Add it to this page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you find a statement that belongs on the site but lack a proof, you are encouraged to add the item (presumably to the appropriate 'wanted proofs' or similar page) so others can contribute a proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Editing: comprehensive general documentation; good first read
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the Editing help page for general, comprehensive documentation about editing ProofWiki; recommended as the initial resource for new contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page Editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Page Editing: details on how ProofWiki pages are to be structured
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Page Editing help page for the site-specific structure conventions (how theorem/definition/proof pages should be organized).

rubrics_metrics.name: Source citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Source citations: how to refer to source works
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Source citations help page for the recommended way to cite books, papers, and other sources used in articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories: how to structure ProofWiki by categories
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Categories help page to learn how to categorize pages so they appear in the site index and relevant category trees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disambiguation
rubrics_metrics.description: Disambiguation: how to deal with ambiguous names for theorems and definitions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Disambiguation help page when multiple concepts share a name; use disambiguation pages or specific naming conventions as instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wiki Editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Wiki Editing: dealing with the MediaWiki architecture
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the Wiki Editing help page for instructions about the MediaWiki mechanics used by ProofWiki (editing tools, page histories, namespaces, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Redirects
rubrics_metrics.description: Redirects: how to redirect a page to another
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Redirects help page to learn the proper way to create and manage page redirects instead of duplicating content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Transclusion: how to include the contents of a page on another
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Transclusion help page for how to include templates or page content in multiple pages via transclusion rather than copying.

rubrics_metrics.name: ProofWiki Extension
rubrics_metrics.description: ProofWiki Extension: documentation of ProofWiki-specific extensions of MediaWiki
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the ProofWiki Extension documentation for any site-specific MediaWiki extensions and how to use them correctly in pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX Editing
rubrics_metrics.description: LaTeX Editing: how to typeset mathematics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the LaTeX Editing help page to learn the site-preferred methods for typesetting mathematical expressions and environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: House Style
rubrics_metrics.description: House Style: information on ProofWiki-specific rules and conventions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the House Style help page for conventions about notation, naming, proof presentation, and other editorial standards specific to ProofWiki.

rubrics_metrics.name: Templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Templates: documentation of various templates that are commonly used on ProofWiki
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Templates help page to learn available templates (infoboxes, theorem/proof formatting, warnings, etc.) and how to apply them consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAQs
rubrics_metrics.description: FAQs: For a list of Frequently Asked Questions, check the FAQ page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the FAQ page for quick answers to common newcomer questions about site practices and editing.
